Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Jamie-s-m
Message:
Fix Payme payment race conditions, admin course-list regression, and a privacy leak found in a second security audit

- Make Payme PerformTransaction/CancelTransaction atomic and state-guarded
  (findOneAndUpdate instead of read-then-save), closing a real race where a
  concurrent Perform+Cancel could desync a granted subscription from the
  transaction record; handle a concurrent CreateTransaction duplicate-key
  retry as an idempotent replay instead of a system error; compare the
  webhook's Basic-auth password with a constant-time check.
- Fix a regression from tonight's own draft-by-default change: the admin
  Control Center listed courses via the public isPublished-only endpoint, so
  a new or unpublished course vanished and could never be published from
  there again. Add an admin-scoped all-courses endpoint.
- Fix a regression from tonight's own billing.provider field: a subscriber
  who was already active via Stripe before this deploy had no provider value
  stored, so they fell through to a live "Subscribe" button that could start
  a duplicate paid subscription.
- Fix GET /groups leaking every pending join-requester's name and email to
  any authenticated user, not just that group's teacher/moderators.
- Fix several dangling-reference crashes (exercise/lesson access once a
  course is deleted) using the same guard pattern already applied elsewhere.
- Restrict teacher-application approval to admins only - a moderator scoped
  to limitedUserManagement could otherwise grant the teacher role, which is
  a bigger privilege change than that permission is meant to cover.
- Cascade-clean a deleted user's references (group membership/moderation,
  family links, progress) instead of leaving them dangling.
- Fix CI: add the test-only PAYME_MERCHANT_KEY the new Payme test suite
  needs (was failing the whole pipeline before deploy-render could run), and
  escape an apostrophe that was a real ESLint error, not a warning.
- Correct a stale root .env.example that named the Payme webhook secret
  wrong (PAYME_SECRET_KEY instead of PAYME_MERCHANT_KEY) and didn't document
  the new PAYME_CHECKOUT_URL at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
